title: RNA extraction from Sterivex using phenol:chloroform
author: Helena Pound
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bhu6j6ze
materials: Replace luer-lock cap and vortex for 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare Solution A
steps.instruction: Prepare Solution A by mixing the following components: 750 μL of 20% SDS, 600 μL of 0.5M EDTA, 200 μL of 3M sodium acetate, and 28.45 mL of nuclease free water.

steps.title: Prepare Sterivex for Lysis
steps.instruction: Load the Sterivex filter with lysis beads and Solution A.

substeps.instruction: Remove luer-lock cap from Sterivex.
Carefully pour beads from Bashing Bead Lysis tube into the Sterivex.
Add 700 µL of Solution A to Sterivex.
Return Sterivex to ice, luer-lock side down, to allow bubbles to dissipate.

steps.title: Extract Liquid from Sterivex
steps.instruction: Remove the filter and recover the liquid into the original Bashing Bead lysis tube.

substeps.instruction: Use pliers to squeeze around the end of the Sterivex (opposite from the luer-lock) until it pops apart.
Remove the end with the internal filter attached.
Insert pipette past the neck of the Sterivex before ejecting liquid to pipette all liquid from the Sterivex into the original Bashing Bead lysis tube (save the tube).

steps.title: Perform Phenol-Chloroform Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract RNA using acid phenol:chloroform:IAA and bead beating.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL acid phenol:chloroform:IAA (125:24:1; pH 4.8) to the BashingBead tube, pulling from the bottom layer of the thawed mixture.
Beat on maximum speed for 40 s in bead beater and place on ice briefly to chill.
Spin at maximum speed in a 4 °C benchtop centrifuge for 5 minutes.
Pull off as much of the aqueous supernatant as possible and place in a new 2 mL centrifuge tube.
If a large white protein layer exists between the top and bottom layers, repeat the 500 µL acid phenol:chloroform:IAA addition, vortex, centrifuge, and add supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Remove Residual Phenol
steps.instruction: Clean the aqueous layer using chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 μL chloroform to the aqueous layer.
Vortex well and spin at max speed for 5 min.
Repeat chloroform extraction if necessary to remove residual phenol.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA
steps.instruction: Precipitate the nucleic acids using sodium acetate and ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Add sodium acetate to reach a concentration of ~0.3 M (e.g., for 500 μL recovery, add 50 μL of 3M NaAc) and mix.
Add 2-2.5x volumes of ice cold 100% ethanol (typically filling the rest of a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube) and mix well.
Place in -80 °C freezer for at least 1 hr.
Spin at maximum speed at 0 °C for at least 30 min in a refrigerated centrifuge (spin for 1 hr if low yields are suspected).

steps.title: Wash RNA Pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet with 70% ethanol to remove salts.

substeps.instruction: Carefully decant 100% ethanol without disturbing the pellet.
Wash pellet by adding 1 mL of ice cold 70% ethanol and gently pipetting up and down to dislodge the pellet.
Spin at maximum speed at 0 °C for 15 minutes (spin for 30 minutes if low yields are expected).
Gently aspirate as much of the 70% ethanol as possible using a small pipette tip, taking caution not to aspirate the pellet.

steps.title: Dry and Dissolve Pellet
steps.instruction: Evaporate remaining ethanol and resuspend the RNA.

substeps.instruction: Place the open tube in a 37 °C heating block for about 3-5 min to evaporate all ethanol (ideally in a sterile environment).
Dissolve the RNA (or DNA) pellet in the appropriate amount of RNAse/DNase-free water based on expected yields and needed final concentration.
